title: Contractions and Courtesy
text:
Elizabethan writers freely shortened words in verse and dialogue, producing forms such as 'tis, 'twas and e'en. Such contractions served the metre of a line, but they also signalled a relaxed register that could easily slide into familiarity. A playwright who wished to show a character's rough manners might scatter these clipped forms through his speech, while a courtier would avoid them entirely.

The social meaning of these forms was therefore never purely phonetic. Audiences recognised the difference between a polished address and a careless one at once, and the choice of contraction could reveal class, education or affection. For this reason, modern editors who expand every contraction flatten the characterisation, removing signals that the original audience would have heard at once.

questions.text: According to the first paragraph, why did Elizabethan writers shorten words?
options: To serve the metre of a line

questions.text: According to the first paragraph, what might a playwright use clipped forms to show?
What does the passage imply about the social meaning of contractions?
options: They could reveal class, education or affection
They were used only by courtiers
They had no effect on audiences

questions.text: Why might modern editors who expand every contraction be criticised?
options: Because they remove characterisation signals the original audience would have heard

paragraph_translations: የኤልዛቤት ዘመን ጸሐፊዎች በግጥምና በንግግር ቃላትን በነጻነት ያሳጥሩ ነበር፤ ለምሳሌ 'tis፣ 'twas እና e'en የመሰሉ ቅርጾች ይፈጠሩ ነበር። እንዲህ ያሉ ቅነሳዎች የመስመርን ምት ያገለግሉ ነበር፤ ነገር ግን ወደ ቅርበት በቀላሉ ሊንሸራተት የሚችል ዘና ያለ የአነጋገር ደረጃን ያመለክቱ ነበር። ጥቅል ሰውን ባሕሪ ለማሳየት የፈለገ ተውኔት ጸሐፊ እንዲህ ያሉ ቅርጾችን በንግግሩ ውስጥ ሊበትን ይችላል፤ የቤተ መንግሥት ሰው ግን ፈጽሞ ያስወግዳቸዋል።

የእነዚህ ቅርጾች ማኅበራዊ ትርጉም ፈጽሞ በድምፅ ብቻ የተወሰነ አልነበረም። ታዳሚዎች የተጣራ አነጋገርንና ግድየለሽ አነጋገርን ወዲያውኑ ይለያሉ፤ የቅነሳ ምርጫም መደብን፣ ትምህርትንና ፍቅርን ሊገልጥ ይችላል። ለዚህ ነው ዘመናዊ አርታኢዎች ሁሉንም ቅነሳ የሚያሰፉት ገጸ-ባሕሪውን ያደበዝዛሉ፤ የዋናው ታዳሚ ወዲያውኑ የሚሰማቸውን ምልክቶች ያስወግዳሉ።
